gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the same false UCP assertion: constancy on an arbitrary set, including a null set, is insufficient, and it gives the required nonempty-open/interior condition for the application.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the failure to impose a nonempty-interior constancy region in the UCP, which makes the theorem false and invalidates the kernel-data exclusion until an open ball or equivalent condition is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: The UCP wrongly treats constancy on any subset as implying global constancy; the theorem and its anomaly-domain application require a nonempty open region or contained ball.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives a null-set counterexample, states that unique continuation requires a nonempty open set, explains the affected kernel argument, and supplies the open-set repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 identifies that the perturbation proposition is applied to a general bounded noise operator even though the ordered real-eigenvalue bound requires the relevant self-adjoint spectral setting, and it supplies the corresponding hypothesis repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the missing self-adjoint spectral hypothesis for the noisy operator: arbitrary bounded noise can produce nonreal eigenvalues and destroy the ordered eigenvalue sequence required by the perturbation bound and noisy-spectrum selection.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposition assumes an ordered real-eigenvalue perturbation setting that is not guaranteed when the admitted noise is merely bounded; bounded nonself-adjoint perturbations can produce nonreal eigenvalues, invalidating the noisy spectral construction.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that general bounded noise may make the operator nonseladjoint with complex eigenvalues and no decreasing order, identifies the proposition as unsupported, and requires self-adjoint noise as repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-007 concerns deriving a pointwise density threshold from integrated-power bounds and symbol ambiguity. It does not identify the distinct noisy-versus-clean eigenpair mismatch or the missing unknown noise quadratic term required for the noisy threshold bounds.

ISSUE-007 identifies the same invalid inference: an integrated-power bound cannot prescribe the pointwise density threshold or the resulting sublevel set. Its repair separates the integral target from the density threshold and uses an integral condition, matching the gold concern.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose that the total integral of the power density does not determine a pointwise level or the associated sublevel reconstruction, so the claimed epsilon formula does not follow from the integrated-power estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The equality of a pointwise threshold with an alpha-scaled total-power quadratic form does not follow from integrated bounds; spatial distributions with the same integral can yield different pointwise sublevel sets, requiring a separate level and cumulative-power condition.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes the pointwise density threshold from the integrated power, calls the deduction a non sequitur, explains the resulting reconstruction failure, and proposes renaming the threshold and imposing the integral condition.
